# Unit economics by business model

The aim is not to forecast a company precisely from desk research. The aim is to determine whether a plausible model exists and expose the assumptions that deserve a test.

## Common rules

- Every value is tagged **SOURCED**, **CALCULATED** or **ASSUMED**.
- Show currency, period and whether taxes are included.
- Use ranges where price/cost variability is material.
- Separate revenue, gross contribution, operating profit and founder compensation.
- Include founder time even if it is unpaid. An idea that “makes money” only by ignoring labor may be a low-paid job rather than a scalable business.
- Include acquisition, onboarding, implementation, support, refund/return, payment, platform and compliance costs where relevant.
- Do not infer a customer acquisition cost from ad CPM/CPC alone. Conversion through the actual funnel is still an assumption.
- Use no invented typical conversion rate. If unknown, model sensitivity across explicit scenarios and label them illustrative.

## B2B software / micro-SaaS

Capture:
- buyer and budget owner;
- price per account/location/workflow/seat;
- setup and integration effort;
- hosting, storage, API/LLM, support and security cost;
- sales cycle and procurement friction;
- churn/retention assumptions;
- first 10 customer acquisition route;
- enterprise reliability/compliance requirements.

For a new idea, the first useful calculation is often: contribution per customer per month after direct service and support costs, and number of customers needed to cover fixed costs. Do not assume subscription retention until evidenced.

## B2C / consumer utilities

Capture:
- trigger frequency and repeat use;
- why free alternatives do not satisfy the job;
- purchase friction, trust and privacy concerns;
- one-time vs subscription fit;
- distribution and platform dependency;
- support/refunds/store fees and marginal service cost;
- whether customer value recurs often enough for retention.

Rare events and low-priced one-off purchases require a credible low-cost distribution path or a different monetisation model. Do not assume viral growth.

## Services / agencies / managed operations

Capture:
- price per project or period;
- delivery hours, specialist time and customer onboarding;
- rework, travel, materials, insurance and liability;
- realistic billable capacity and founder salary;
- standardisation/repeatability;
- route to first 10 buyers.

Estimate contribution after delivery labor, not only cash outlay.

## Ecommerce / resale / distribution

Capture:
- product cost, freight, duties/taxes, packaging, storage, payment fees and platform commission;
- return, warranty, damage, fraud and support costs;
- inventory turn, minimum order quantity, supplier terms and working capital;
- channel concentration and price competition;
- any required certifications or safety rules.

Do not call gross margin “profit”. Model stock that does not sell and cash locked before receiving payment.

## Physical products / manufacturing

Capture:
- customer type and actual specification/purchase need;
- bill of materials or estimated landed cost, with quote provenance;
- tooling, samples, minimum order quantities, scrap/quality failure and capacity;
- lead times, working capital, payment terms and supplier concentration;
- certifications, warranty, installation, returns and product liability;
- how buyers currently source the item and how they choose vendors.

Desk research rarely proves manufacturing economics. Mark supplier quotes and buyer orders as required real-world validation.

## Marketplace / aggregator

Capture both sides of the market:
- who supplies and who pays;
- supply onboarding and demand acquisition cost;
- frequency, take rate, payment disputes, refunds and leakage/off-platform transactions;
- liquidity by geography/segment;
- regulatory liability and service quality.

Do not model gross transaction value as revenue.

## Info product / training / licensing

Capture:
- who has the need and why existing free material is insufficient;
- content creation and update burden;
- trust/credibility requirements;
- distribution, refund/chargeback and support costs;
- how the offer differs from free search, open-source documentation and AI assistance.

## Minimum scenario table

For any shortlisted idea, provide:

| Input | Downside | Base | Upside | Evidence status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Price or revenue per unit | | | | |
| Units/customers attainable in period | | | | |
| Variable delivery cost | | | | |
| Acquisition cost or founder acquisition hours | | | | |
| Contribution after variable costs | | | | |
| Fixed costs / compliance / capital needs | | | | |
| Founder hours per period | | | | |

If inputs cannot be responsibly estimated, replace fake scenarios with a list of the 3–5 unknown inputs and the cheapest way to discover each.
